I will think this through like the old farmer I am.

My land is 10.1 mu. My legs aren't what they used to be, and cotton takes too much bending and picking. I used to plant more cotton, but now I keep only 2 mu of cotton — just enough to sell for some cash. The rest, 8.1 mu, I do wheat then maize like always. My father did it, my neighbors do it, and the land gives back well.

For wheat, I sow in October. I use the improved seed the dealer brings — 济麦 type, I forget the number, but the bag is the one most people in the village buy. I put down two bags of 复合肥 (compound fertilizer, 15-15-15) per mu before ploughing, that's about 50 kg, so roughly 7-8 kg of each. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. So in total for nitrogen I am around 18 kg, phosphorus maybe 8 kg, potassium 8 kg. I water the wheat at planting, then at 返青 (green-up), at 拔节 (jointing), and at 灌浆 (grain filling) — 4 times. Pesticide I spray 2 times, once for 蚜虫 (aphids) and once mixed for 白粉 and 赤霉 when I see trouble. The well is nearby so water is not a big worry, only the electricity cost.

For maize after wheat, I sow right after harvest in June, 郑单958 or whatever hybrid seed is going. I put compound fertilizer with the seed, about 40 kg per mu, then top-dress urea 20 kg at 大喇叭口 (big trumpet stage). That is nitrogen maybe 20 kg, phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 6 kg. Maize does not need much water here in summer if rain comes — I irrigate once or twice. Pesticide once or twice for 玉米螟 (corn borer). Tillage I do rotary, it is faster and the wheat stubble is not too much.

For cotton on my 2 mu, I use Bt hybrid seed — everybody uses it, bollworm does not eat it. I put 40 kg compound fertilizer as base, then topdress urea 20 kg at flowering. Cotton eats more potassium so I add a bag of potassium too. I water 3 times. Pesticide I still spray 5 times even with Bt — for 盲蝽 (mirid bugs), 蚜虫, red spider. Cotton is troublesome but the price is okay. I plough for cotton, deeper is better.

I keep to what worked last year. Fertilizer costs money but a thin crop costs more.
